messages:
sara: Heads-up — we need a runbook for large-scale rekeying (customer data envelope keys) after the CMK rotation next week. Questions: progress tracking, throttling against KMS, and recovery for partial failures.

mike: +1. Are we using AWS KMS ReEncrypt API or do we have local DEKs we rewrap ourselves? That changes design.

amal: For most customer blobs we use envelope encryption with locally stored encrypted DEKs (ciphertext DEK stored with object). We rewrap the DEK, not the payload. So ReEncrypt (server-side) only applies if ciphertext was produced by KMS.

sara: Right — mixed estate. Some older flows used AWS GenerateDataKey + store ciphertext; others used E2EE with client-side DEKs. Need patterns for both.

jen: For AWS-specific: if ciphertext DEK was produced by KMS (we have CMK ARN recorded), we can call kms:ReEncrypt from a worker with appropriate role. But we must throttle to avoid throttling exceptions and also ensure CloudTrail shows each rewrap.

kevin: Re: audit — do not log plaintext DEKs or payloads. Log only event metadata: object_id, old_key_arn, new_key_arn, status, worker_id, timestamp, error_code (if any). Store events in audit index.

mike: Implementation notes I suggested in the ticket: 1) checkpoint at object-level (last_processed_id) + per-shard queues, 2) use token bucket throttler per-KMS-key per-region, 3) exponential backoff on 5xx/Throttling, special handling for KMS LimitExceeded vs AccessDenied.

amal: Also need idempotency: workers should include a conditional check that the stored ciphertext-DEK still references old_key_arn before rewrap, and update atomically. Use DB compare-and-swap or write a per-object rewrap status flag.

sara: Sample pseudo CLI I posted previously for AWS ReEncrypt: 
```
aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://enc_dek.bin --destination-key-id arn:aws:kms:...:key/new 
```
But in-code we'd call ReEncrypt with context and EncryptionContext for audit.

jen: For GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault: GCP has 'cryptoKeys: reencrypt' equiv? GCP supports 'decrypt' + 'encrypt' calls on KMS; they don't expose a single rewrap RPC, so rewrap worker must call Asymmetric/Decrypt+Encrypt or do DEK decrypt+encrypt in worker. Azure Key Vault has 'wrapKey'/'unwrapKey' endpoints — same pattern. Design must avoid plaintext DEK exposure outside trusted environment.

kevin: Operational concerns: global rate limits per-account for KMS APIs. We need to surface per-region budgets in the console so ops can pause/resume per-region. Also alert on >x% of rewrap tasks failing in a window.

mike: Throttling strategy: dynamic token bucket sized from KMS SLA: start with conservative QPS (e.g., 100 reqs/s per region) and ramp up by 2x every 10 minutes until error rate increases above 1%. Use metrics: KMS_ThrottleRate, Rewrap_ErrorRate, Rewrap_Latency.

amal: Recovery patterns: if worker crashes mid-rewrap, ensure the object either 1) still references old_key_arn (so worker can retry), or 2) has a tombstone stage where stage="in_progress" with worker_id and TTL. If TTL expires, another worker can take-over after verifying idempotency.

jen: We should avoid long DB txns. Proposed atomic update flow: 
1) read object metadata row: {enc_dek, key_arn} 
2) call KMS ReEncrypt or wrap/unwrap -> new_enc_dek (retry with backoff, but don't hold locks) 
3) CAS update metadata adding new_enc_dek and new_key_arn only if key_arn == old_key_arn 
4) if CAS fails, discard new_enc_dek and increment conflict metric

kevin: For auditing, emit two events: pre-rewrap (object_id, old_arn, attempt_id) and post-rewrap (object_id, new_arn, attempt_id, duration, outcome). Tie attempt_id to worker so we can trace. Store these in append-only audit store.

sara: Edge cases: cross-account CMK moves, key policy denials mid-run, and automatic key deletion/disable. Need pre-check phase to validate new_key_arn exists and is enabled and that service principal has kms:ReEncrypt (or wrap/unwrap) on both keys.

mike: Can we run a dry-run to surface objects that will fail? e.g., check access for each unique key_arn by calling KMS:DescribeKey and TestKeyMaterial (or call Verify‑permissions via IAM simulator).

amal: We also need to handle multi-region keys and multi-variant: if data stored in us-west-2 but new CMK is in us-east-1, ReEncrypt may be cross-region and slower or disallowed. Prefer region-local new keys or route rewrap to same region.

kevin: Metrics & progress: emit per-shard counts (processed, success, failed, pending) and a global estimated completion ETA based on throughput. Expose a small UI with pause/resume and per-key throttle knobs.

jen: Example failure log snippet we saw in testing: 
```
ERROR rewrap-worker-12 object=acct-123/blob-987 err=LimitExceeded KMS request rate exceeded retry_after=250ms
```
Worker should increment metric and sleep + jitter. If repeated 429/LimitExceeded for >30s, mark the key as throttled and back off globally.

amal: For client-side DEKs (we are the only party holding plaintext data keys): re-encrypt locally without calling KMS at all if rekeying only rotates envelope KEK (we might rewrap DEKs using our own HSM). But if rotating external CMK we must use KMS wrap/unwrap. Document both flows.

kevin: Security note: never store attempt logs with the raw DEK or plaintext sizes. ACL audit should be strict; only sec team and ops can trigger full debug.

sara: Action items: 
- Mike: draft runbook steps + pseudocode for CAS flow (due EOD)
- Amal: prototype token-bucket throttler and TTL-based takeover logic (due tomorrow)
- Jen: write audit-event schema and retention policy for rewrap events (due tomorrow)
- Kevin: enumerate KMS API rate limits per cloud and propose default throttles (due EOD)

mike: quick Q — should the rewrap job be RBAC-protected behind a feature flag and gated by an approval workflow? I think yes for enterprise customers.

kevin: Yes — gate runbook via RBAC + approval (once-off) in console. Record approver and justification in audit event.

keykeeper-bot: Scheduled rekey maintenance window is set for 2025-05-02T02:00Z. Current job status: NOT_STARTED. Reminder: update runbook link.

sara: thanks all. I'll collate notes and post a tidy runbook draft to the security runbooks space. If anyone has test vectors (objects with old_key_arns, conflicting CAS states) drop them here. :sparkles:
